results.name: frozen_zero
results.description: Clear only frozen flag in copied snapshot

results.name: commit_mismatch
results.description: Change one commit without changing sequence/index
results.rejection: every slot commit and physical index agree

results.name: missing_marker
results.description: Change first marker to another event while retaining commit/sequence
results.rejection: both original marker payloads survived actual fault

results.name: raw_opcode_wrong_address
results.description: Keep UDF opcode but move the raw target read address by two bytes
results.rejection: raw target UDF opcode read at the actual fault PC

results.name: wrong_delay_budget
results.description: Change retained delay budget from two to three ticks

results.name: wrong_task
results.description: Retain the whole six-event timeline but attribute it to a different task
results.rejection: markers identify the actual faulting task

results.name: huge_sequence_range
results.description: Increase next sequence before any range allocation

results.name: wrong_elf_argument
results.description: Change actual debugger symbol argument while keeping firmware hash field
results.rejection: actual debugger ELF and script arguments

results.name: wrong_stlink_serial
results.description: Select a different ST-LINK in copied server arguments

results.name: missing_attach_confirmation
results.description: Remove Attach confirmation from the copied server log

result.scope: Physical F446 SWD SRAM and target opcode, after verified UART fault capture

limits: Three samples per path; no statistical confidence or WCET guarantee
Samples include loop, scheduler and SysTick interference
Symbols do not fully attribute inline call-site or alignment cost
ON/OFF performance does not itself prove an absence of all bugs
Native model is not an ARM interrupt emulator or sanitizer
M7 checks are code generation only, not hardware validation
Frozen bounded history can lose an old WAIT and must report UNKNOWN
Terminal fault SRAM is not persistent across reset/power loss
Performance samples are complete-work measurements, not WCET
Historical intermediate/failed attempts are not counted as final passes
